title: wringer.gate-artifacts.v1
description:
`gates/NNN_<id>/artifacts.json` — what one gate left for a PERSON to look at. A SIBLING file, never a relabel: `gate-result.schema.json` is closed over nine fields with `additionalProperties: false`, `result.json` gains no field and changes no meaning, and law 7 always allows a new schema file. The same shape `digests.json` and `briefed.json` already use.

**THE ABSENCE OF THIS FILE IS THE COMPATIBILITY BOUNDARY.** Every bundle written before it existed, and every gate that leaves no artifact, reads exactly as it did before.

**NOTHING HERE IS REDACTED IF IT IS BINARY, AND THAT CANNOT BE FIXED.** `redact.py` erases the VALUES of environment variables whose NAMES match `*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`, `*KEY*` and whatever the repository adds, by substring replacement. That is a text operation. A screenshot can carry a token rendered on a page, a customer's name in a fixture, or an API key in a URL bar, and no pattern in `.wringer.yaml` will remove any of it. Every row says which kind it is. Artifacts are therefore OPT-IN PER GATE — turning them on is a repository declaring that this gate's output is shareable — and they never leave the machine by default: not in an MR body, not in an attestation payload, not in anything `wring deliver --send` transmits.

**The harness records a name, a size, a digest and a media type. It does not caption, label or interpret.** Nothing in this file is a claim about what an artifact SHOWS.

gate.description: The id of the gate that left these.

artifacts.description: Every file recorded, in sorted order so two runs over the same files produce byte-identical records. Empty when a gate opted in and left only omissions.

name.description: Path relative to the gate's `artifacts/` directory.

bytes.description: Size AS RECORDED — after redaction for a text artifact, which can change it.

sha256.description: Digest of the bytes on disk. `evidence.digest_directory` also covers this file and every artifact, and `wring audit` catches added, missing and altered ones, so no new verification path exists.

media_type.description: From a CLOSED allow-list keyed on the extension. Closed because 'whatever the extension says' is how an unexpected type reaches a renderer.

redacted.description: Whether this artifact went through the same scrub as any other captured text. FALSE for every binary, always, and that is a statement about what is possible rather than about what was configured. A row claiming `true` for a file whose bytes are not decodable text would be the format lying, so the writer trusts the bytes over the extension.

omitted.description: What was left out, and why. OMITTED AND NAMED, NEVER TRUNCATED: a truncated image is a corrupt image that still reads as evidence, and `stdout_truncated` works only because text survives truncation. Absence is stated here rather than being invisible. Deliberately not called 'refused' — in this codebase a `Refused` is a hard stop with an exit code, and an omission is not one.

reason.description: `too_large`: over the per-artifact cap. `total_exceeded`: it would have taken the run over its declared total. `unknown_type`: its extension is not on the allow-list. `unreadable`: it could not be read.

bytes.description: Present when the size is known and is the reason.

limits.description: What this record does NOT say, travelling with it rather than living in a spec nobody opened — the `acceptance.json` precedent.
